Does not give a constructive machine proof of the real/rational monotone convergence theorem being equivalent to LPO: Mathlib's Q depends on Classical.choice (Rat.le_total, audited), so the rational side is only a classical bridge for the Zeno readings; the real form is cited literature (Mandelkern 1988 via Diener 2020).

scope: C-418: without Classical.choice (machine-asserted by a Lean.collectAxioms audit that fails compilation otherwise), LimBit (every monotone Boolean sequence has a settling step) <-> LPO, NatBMC (every bounded monotone natural-number sequence has a settling step) <-> LPO, and without boundedness the settling principle is false (x n = n). C-419: the Zeno reading zenoReading k n = 2^k - 2^(k-n) settles at step k (explicit formula), its settled value plus one is 2^k, every reading is below 2^k, and it is monotone, all without Classical.choice; bridge (classical, Mathlib Q): zenoReading k n = floor(2^k * (1 - (1/2)^n)), the rational Zeno sequence is monotone, below 1, within (1/2)^k of 1 from step k, and Cauchy with explicit step k+1. C-420 (classical): for every partial recursive code e the stage-halting bit sequence haltBits e is monotone and classically has a settling step, but no computable F gives a settling step for all e and no computable f gives the final value (Mathlib halting problem). C-421 (classical): LPO holds classically (from excluded middle), every halting statement is decided by excluded middle, the halting set and the even numbers both exist as sets, evenness is computable and halting is not.
